text: **CertGate prepares the review of a steel mill inspection certificate against a purchase specification, and proposes release, block or review.
A person in Quality decides.** CertGate never releases material on its own.

**All data in this repository is fictitious.** Siderúrgica Valdemora S.A. (the mill), Talleres Ribera Norte S.L. (the buyer), the grade TRN-355 and the purchase specification ESP-014 are invented for the demo.
The limits in ESP-014 belong to that fictitious company and are **not** the limits of any real standard.
Only these synthetic certificates are ever sent to the model endpoint.

Companion documents: [METRICS.md](METRICS.md) (evaluation, generated) · [DEPLOY.md](DEPLOY.md) (Vercel, for the human) · [CLAIMS.md](CLAIMS.md) (every capability sentence and its proof) · [EVIDENCE-INDEX.md](EVIDENCE-INDEX.md) (where the evidence is).

When a batch of steel arrives at a plant, it comes with a mill certificate (an inspection certificate of the EN 10204 3.1 kind): heat or lot, grade, chemical composition and measured mechanical properties.

text: **Primary user:** goods-in or Quality technician at a mid-size plant that buys certified material.
**Who decides:** the Quality manager who signs the release or the block.
For each case (certificate PDF plus its delivery-note line), CertGate:
row: none: lead-in to the list that follows

text: Validates the files (PDF by magic bytes, size limits, not encrypted, has pages) and records their SHA-256.
Reads the certificate through two channels:
row: none: lead-in to the list that follows

text: the **model channel**: the open model Qwen3.8-27B, served by AMD Token Factory, reads the rendered **page images** of every certificate, digital or scanned, and returns the values as one JSON object;
the **text layer** of a digital PDF, extracted without any model.
A scan has no text layer, so its critical fields need human confirmation, and CertGate says so.
Compares the channels.
A disagreement makes the field unknown and the case goes to review.
Checks internal coherence: heat or lot against the delivery note, expected units and scale jumps, and the printed carbon equivalent against one recomputed from the composition.
The formula's source is cited in [docs/sources/cev-formula.md](docs/sources/cev-formula.md).
Applies deterministic, versioned rules against the spec, with exact decimals (never binary floating point).
Proposes `release`, `block` or `review`, records the person's decision (who, when, why) and exports a run receipt without secrets.
Proposal precedence: a heat mismatch means review; otherwise block > review > release.
Release is proposed only when no review or block condition holds.
A scan is never proposed for release until a person has confirmed every critical field.
**Endpoint:** AMD Token Factory, the AMD compute of the event (OpenAI-compatible; host `developer.amd.com.cn`).

**Model:** requested as `Qwen3.8-27B`; every reply reports it as `self-dploy/Qwen3.8-27B`. Its publisher is the Qwen Team, and its licence, as published by the publisher, is apache-2.0 (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, retrieved 2026-10-13; see [docs/sources/model.md](docs/sources/model.md)).
**What the model does:** it reads the page images of a certificate into the CertGate reading contract: value, unit, status, and the location where it says it found the value.
Requests use temperature 0 and a frozen instruction (SHA-256 `32fad2f9…`).
**What the model never does:** it never decides and never explains.
The text-layer comparison, the coherence checks, the rules and the proposal run in the CertGate backend without any model, and a person decides.
The model's reasoning text is never used or stored.
**How it is shown:**

text: The "Runs on AMD" panel (`#/amd`) shows only what the endpoint reports: the model list, the key's rate limit and daily spend, and the latency, tokens and cost of the last reading.
Every receipt of a real reading (live or recorded) carries a copy of those values from reading time, plus the endpoint reply's id, created time, model and usage.
The endpoint does not expose the GPU model, the ROCm version or the serving-stack version.
With the endpoint on, the panel says "not exposed by the endpoint" for them; with it off, they show "unknown", like the other endpoint values (the model list shows "none").
Nothing else claims them.
**Cost:** the cost shown is the cost reported by the endpoint; Token Factory credits are free and have no monetary value.
Two independent real runs read the same 27 fictitious certificates (cg-004 … cg-030). cg-001 … cg-003 were used to tune the prompt and are excluded.
Every figure comes from the committed run artifacts.

Input limits:
row: none: lead-in to the list that follows

text: CLI and container: certificate PDF up to 10 MiB; delivery note up to 1 MiB.
Web upload: **up to 3 MiB** of PDF, sent as base64 so the request stays below Vercel's 4.5 MB body limit; delivery note up to 256 KiB.
**Shared service.** AMD Token Factory is a shared service.
Per key: about 20–30 requests per minute, 8 concurrent requests, and a rolling daily spend cap read from GET /usage (1, in free credits).
During the human's test it answered 429 (concurrency), 504 from the upstream, and connection timeouts.
In the band's two evaluation runs there were 0 retries and 0 failures.
CertGate keeps at most 2 requests in flight, retries only 429 and 5xx (at most 3 attempts, Retry-After honoured), and waits up to 300 s per attempt.
The provider keeps prompts and outputs for about 2 days, so only synthetic data may be sent.
Before any live reading the page shows that notice, and the server requires the visitor to confirm it.
**Slow readings.** One reading takes about 1 to 4 minutes (52–208 s per certificate in the evaluation).
**Uploads.** Without `LIVE_ACCESS_CODE`, live reading is limited to the 30 dataset certificates, matched by SHA-256; with it, a visitor's synthetic file can also be read.
The access-code path is tested against a local stub with a test-only code, and no real access code is configured on the band's host.
**cg-003, the ambiguous scan.** The model reads the smudged yield strength confidently as **338** MPa; the true value is 358.
It did so in both completed tuning reads, in the recorded story and in the adversary's probe.
The product therefore proposes **block** (rule failure plus no second channel), never release, and the scan still needs a person to confirm every critical field.
The story card shows what the recorded run shows.
The prompt was not tuned to change this.
**Decimal comma, no unit.** The model sometimes returns a printed CEV with a decimal comma and no unit (`0,41`).
It happened once in each real run, on a different case each time (cg-028 in the implementer run, cg-004 in the auditor's).
The text-layer channel check caught it every time, and the case went to review.
**No model-written explanation.** The model is not asked for an explanation, and the product never shows one.
This deviates from step 7 of the product design (03-DISENO); it was chosen to keep decisions entirely in the deterministic rules (I1).
The case file shows the rule reasons.
**Locations are the model's claim.** The page and fragment where the model says it found a value are labelled "as reported by the model" and are not verified.
On digital PDFs the text layer checks the values, not the locations.
**Hostile duplicate field.** A text layer with a spoofed duplicate of a field (cg-022: "ReH (MPa) 400" while the table says 340) makes that field unknown.
A would-be block becomes review, never release.
**Prompt examples.** The reading instruction's examples reuse values of cg-001 ("0.16", "392", "QA-07"). cg-001 is a tuning and story case, outside the 27-case evaluation.
**Text-layer parser.** It covers the two fictitious certificate layouts of the dataset, not arbitrary mill certificates.
**Cosmetic:** `/favicon.ico` answers 404.

text: Real model, real endpoint: each run read 27 fictitious certificates (cg-004 … cg-030) through AMD Token Factory.
Definitions follow register D3-05 as amended by R3.1 C-08 … C-11 and C-15. cg-001 … cg-003 were used to tune the prompt and are excluded from both runs.
The two runs are independent: different seats, different clean checkouts, different times.
The landing page shows the figures of the implementer run, and names that run.
Candidate commits: each run names the commit it actually ran (below).
The accepted Stage 3 candidate is `5c904693`.
Between these commits the reading path is identical by diff: the reader's request and parsing, the frozen prompt and the rules.
The later commits changed receipt contents (the F1 snapshot and the "as reported by the model" location label), the UI, the upload policy and the tests.
**False conforming** (the grave error): FC-broad = proposal release where the expected proposal is not release, over all cases whose expected proposal is not release.
FC-strict = release where the expected proposal is block, over the expected-block cases (C-08).
Any false conforming in any real run is a REJECT finding with a root-cause line (C-19).
**Rule abstention** = proposal review with status processed; **failure** = status error, by class; reported separately, each over all evaluated cases (C-09).

**Per-field accuracy** compares the model channel with the correct reading of each critical field: correct, unknown, wrong, invented (a value where the field is absent), and **confident-on-illegible** (a confident value where the correct reading is illegible), counted separately (C-10).
**Seconds and cost per certificate** are over processed cases (status not error), with N; a missing reported cost is unknown, never zero (C-11).
Requests use **temperature 0** (C-12).
The runs are reported side by side, with every per-case proposal difference listed below; a difference is never hidden behind one passing run.

Receipts and run artifacts carry the endpoint reply's id, created time, model and usage as returned (C-14); GET /usage is read before and after each run and reconciled with the sum of per-reply costs (C-15).
The tuning cases **cg-001, cg-002 and cg-003** are excluded from the evaluation (D3-03); they are the judge-mode stories.

**Live reading:** on the deployed site, when it is configured (DEPLOY.md), or from the container in real mode with the three `MODEL_*` variables (see "Run it").
Download a sample certificate from the live screen, choose it, confirm the third-party notice (and type the access code where one is set), and press "Read live".

The page shows the job as queued with its position, then reading with the seconds so far, then opens the case file; a failed reading says why and offers a retry, and never shows a stored result instead.
In the container, live readings run as jobs with an in-process queue and limits; no store is needed.
On the deployed site they need the access code and the shared store (DEPLOY.md).

| `POST /api/live/read` | `{certificate_base64, delivery_csv?, delivery_line?, access_code?, synthetic_confirmed: true}`: a live reading in one request, container only, or C11 `endpoint_off` with no endpoint; 503 on the deployed site (`no-store`) |

| `POST /api/live/jobs` | `{certificate_base64, delivery_csv?, delivery_line?, synthetic_confirmed: true}`, the access code in the `x-live-access-code` header: starts a live reading job and answers 202 with its id and queue position (`no-store`) |
| `GET /api/live/jobs/<id>` | the job: queued with position, reading with elapsed seconds, done with the view and receipt of its own reading, or failed with a reason class (`no-store`) |
| `GET /api/samples`, `GET /api/samples/<cg-004\|cg-005\|cg-010>/<certificate.pdf\|delivery.csv>` | three dataset certificates and their delivery notes, to download and upload back |
`reader` is `live` when an endpoint and a model are configured outside the deployed site, or on the deployed site when live reading is enabled there, and `off` otherwise.

| `LIVE_READS_PER_HOUR` | none (disabled) | live readings per UTC hour, counted on the server (in the shared store on the deployed site, in process in the container); unset, invalid or 0 = disabled; documented deployment value 20 |
| `LIVE_ACCESS_CODE` | none (no default) | mandatory for live reading on the deployed site; in the container, needed for a visitor-uploaded file (without it only dataset certificates are read live) |
| `LIVE_CODE_FAILURES_PER_HOUR` | `5` | wrong codes allowed per client per UTC hour; other clients’ wrong codes never block a correct code |
| `LIVE_CODE_FAILURES_PER_HOUR` | optional, default `5` | no | wrong codes allowed per client per UTC hour; other clients’ wrong codes never block a correct code (section 6) |
A client (identified by a hash of the address Vercel sets in `x-vercel-forwarded-for`) is refused for the rest of the UTC hour after `LIVE_CODE_FAILURES_PER_HOUR` wrong codes (default 5).

Wrong codes from all clients are also counted together, for monitoring only (`code_failures_this_hour_global` in `/api/live/status`); that count never refuses anyone, so a correct code is never refused because other clients failed.

The residual risk is that guessing spread over many client addresses is bounded only by `LIVE_CODE_FAILURES_PER_HOUR` per address and per hour, so the real barrier is the code itself: set `LIVE_ACCESS_CODE` to a long random value, at least 20 random characters from a password generator.

To clear one client's lockout before the hour ends, delete the key `certgate:live:codefail:c:<hash>:<hour>` in the Upstash console (`certgate:live:codefail:g:<hour>` is the monitoring count), where `<hour>` is the UTC hour as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH`; or wait for the next UTC hour.
| `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` | none | the shared store's REST URL, set by the Vercel Marketplace integration (deployed site only) |
| `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` | none | secret: the shared store's token, set by the integration |
| `KV_REST_API_URL` | none | fallback name of the store URL, read when the Upstash name is absent |
| `KV_REST_API_TOKEN` | none | secret: fallback name of the store token |
| `VERCEL` | set by Vercel | the deployed-site rules: live reading needs the access code, the shared store, an hourly limit and the endpoint |

Sources: [docs/sources/vercel-limits.md](docs/sources/vercel-limits.md), [docs/sources/vercel-functions.md](docs/sources/vercel-functions.md), [docs/sources/upstash-redis.md](docs/sources/upstash-redis.md).
**Live reading on the deployed site is bounded by the function duration (OI-S2-02).**

A job waits at most 60 s for one of the two reading slots and then has at most 210 s to read, inside the 300 s function duration; a reading that does not finish in time fails as "timed out" and offers a retry.

The one-request route `/api/live/read` stays unavailable there (503 "live reading unavailable on the deployed site; live demonstration from the container"); the deployed site reads through the job API.
Without the access code and the shared store configured, the deployed site has no live reading at all.
**Live-read limits (OI-S2-01).** On the deployed site the hourly limit, the two in-flight slots and the wrong-code counts are kept in the shared store, so they hold across all instances.
In the container they are kept in process: two separate container processes with a limit of 2 let 4 readings through (test "the live limit is per instance" in `test/web.test.ts`).
The band does not deploy and holds no Vercel, GitHub or store credentials; the human does this.

text: Judge mode works with no configuration: three recorded real readings, the case files, human confirmation and decision, the receipts, and the landing figures.
Live reading on the deployed site is the extra: it is enabled only when the access code, the shared store, the hourly limit and the model endpoint are all configured (sections 3 and 4).
Without them the site behaves exactly as the Stage 5 site, and makes no model call.

A live reading runs as a job inside that limit (`DEPLOYED_LIVE_BUDGET` in `src/web/limits.ts`): at most 60 s waiting for a reading slot, at most 210 s reading (rendering, attempts and retries included), and 30 s kept free.
The job keeps running after the first answer through Vercel's `waitUntil` ([docs/sources/vercel-functions.md](docs/sources/vercel-functions.md)).
3. The shared store (done by the human on 2026-10-14, about 12:55Z)
Live reading needs one store shared by all function instances, for the queue and the limits.
Connect **Upstash for Redis** from the Vercel Marketplace to the project ([docs/sources/upstash-redis.md](docs/sources/upstash-redis.md)).

In the Vercel project's Environment Variables page, check that **one** of these pairs is present: `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` and `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN`, or `KV_REST_API_URL` and `KV_REST_API_TOKEN`. CertGate reads the first pair, else the second.
It never reads `KV_REST_API_READ_ONLY_TOKEN`.
The Upstash Free plan allows 500K commands per month ([docs/sources/upstash-redis.md](docs/sources/upstash-redis.md)).
One live reading costs about 40 to 60 store commands: about 15 for admission and the code check, one slot attempt every 2 s while it waits, and one poll every 2 s from the browser while it reads.
A judge's reading of 35 s is about 40 commands.
If the store refuses or cannot be reached, live reading is refused with "the shared store is unavailable; live reading refused"; it never falls back to anything else.

Choosing the model for a live reading
Token Factory's model list changes without notice: Gemma-4-31B-IT was listed on 2026-10-13 and absent on 2026-10-15.
So the live screen shows the list as the endpoint gives it now, in three groups:
**Measured:** Qwen3.8-27B and Gemma-4-31B-IT, the only models with an evaluation run in [METRICS.md](METRICS.md).
Each is selectable only while the endpoint lists it, and names its METRICS.md section and run directory.
The default is `MODEL_ID` when it is listed, otherwise the first listed measured model; it is never an experimental model.

**Not evaluated · experimental:** models that, in one real probe on 2026-10-15, accepted CertGate's request (the page image of the scan cg-016 and the frozen prompt) and returned a reply that passed the response schema, named the requested model and finished within 210 s. Four passed: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, MiMo-V2.6-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ([probe evidence](evidence/runs/certgate-001/stage-8/probes/BATCH.md)).
The probe does not judge the values read.

Choosing one needs the acknowledgement "this model is not evaluated; no figure of CertGate applies to it", and its reading is labelled "not evaluated" next to the proposal and in its receipt (`evaluated: false`, with the probe evidence path).
**Listed, not offered:** every other id the endpoint lists, shown disabled with its reason: "no image probe", "probe failed", "not a chat model" or "not enabled on this site".

The server checks the choice again before anything is counted: a model outside the offer, an experimental model without the acknowledgement, or a model the endpoint does not list now is refused before any model call and without spending the hourly limit.
The reply must name the requested model (equal ignoring case, or with one provider prefix such as `self-dploy/`); a reading never falls back to another model or to a stored result.
Every live receipt and its endpoint snapshot record the model requested and the model as reported.
The rules, the two-channel check, the review triggers and the person's decision are the same for every model.
`LIVE_MODELS` (optional) narrows the choice; without it only `MODEL_ID` is selectable.
Live reading uses the model chosen on the live screen, with Vercel's `MODEL_ID` as the default, and each live receipt names the model requested and the model as the endpoint reports it.

4a. The model choice (Stage 8)
With `LIVE_MODELS` set to the value above, the live screen shows every model AMD Token Factory lists now (the same check as "Runs on AMD", at most once per 60 s), in three groups:
**measured** (Qwen3.8-27B, Gemma-4-31B-IT): selectable while listed; the default is `MODEL_ID` when listed;
**not evaluated · experimental** (the four models that passed the Stage 8 probe): selectable while listed, only with the acknowledgement on the page;
**listed, not offered:** every other id, disabled with its reason.
The choice is limited to measured models and to what Token Factory lists now.
A model the endpoint stops listing is shown disabled, and the server refuses it before any model call; nothing falls back to another model.
No redeploy is needed when the list changes.
Without `LIVE_MODELS` only `MODEL_ID` can be chosen.

Then one real live reading **with each offered model the endpoint lists at that time**, in a browser: open the site, go to "Read a certificate live", download the sample cg-004 certificate and its delivery note, choose them, give line 1 and the access code, choose the model (for an experimental model, tick its acknowledgement), tick the notice and press "Read live".

Its receipt names the model requested and the model as reported by the endpoint, with the endpoint snapshot taken at reading time; a reading by an experimental model is labelled "not evaluated" next to its proposal.
Each reading counts once against `LIVE_READS_PER_HOUR`.
